page: Microsoft Azure DC2es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by Intel Xeon TDX processors built on x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core via hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The memory configuration provides 8.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware instruction capabilities include Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), AVX-512 variants, and hardware cryptography features such as AES and SHA-NI. The instance does not include local disk storage or discrete GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates steady single-core execution alongside predictable multi-core scaling limits. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1906.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1671.0, both aligning with middle-tier performance profiles. Due to the single physical core footprint, multi-threaded results are constrained, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 2411.0, stress-ng multi-core registering 1961.87, and Redis SET throughput reaching 2.38 million operations per second. PassMark CPU and database benchmark scores place in lower tiers accordingly.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the DC2es_v6 delivers dedicated compute resources and modern instruction sets with low resource overhead, trading parallel processing capacity for single-threaded predictability. Workload suitability centers on low-concurrency web serving, microservice endpoints, staging environments, API mediation, and lightweight administrative utilities.
description: Microsoft Azure DC2es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical Intel Xeon TDX core running at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration. Advanced vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX are supported, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions. The instance features no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show moderate single-thread compute capabilities, recording 1906.08 in stress-ng single-core and 1671.0 in Geekbench single-core tests, whereas multi-core throughput reflects the physical single-core hardware ceiling with a 2411.0 Geekbench multi-core score. In terms of cost efficiency, it provides an economical baseline for low-demand services that require dedicated CPU execution without high thread concurrency. The DC2es_v6 is well fitted for basic web serving, microservice hosting, development environments, and lightweight background automation tasks.
